candidates.title: LIPS: Rocky Horror LIVE at House of Yes
candidates.time_text: doors 6:30pm, show 7:15pm; seating not guaranteed after 7:30pm
candidates.price_text: from about $58 general admission; cabaret tables cost more
candidates.summary: House of Yes's resident cast performs its own live reimagining of Rocky Horror — drag, burlesque and aerial, not a screening with a shadow cast. The 2026 run is Oct 8, 9, 10, 15, 16, 22 and 23; this week that's Thursday and Friday. Doors 6:30, show 7:15, seated cabaret with table packages available.
candidates.fit: He dressed up for Rocky Horror in Flatbush and loved it, and House of Yes is the one Bushwick room that does spectacle without bro energy. Thursday is his main weeknight slot and the show is done by about 9:30, so he's home at a dad hour.

candidates.title: Petite Rouge
candidates.time_text: evening showtimes vary by night; pick a date on the box office calendar
candidates.summary: Company XIV's world-premiere Baroque Burlesque take on Little Red Riding Hood, running at their own Théâtre XIV in Bushwick and extended through Halloween. Opulent costumes, aerial work, live vocalists, full cocktail service at your seat. Nutcracker Rouge replaces it starting Nov 12, so this run ends Oct 31.
candidates.fit: Company XIV is his favorite company in the city and their Halloween burlesque show was a highlight — this is the current mainstage, and it closes on Halloween. Exactly the polished-but-filthy register that works for a date night with the wife.

candidates.title: hABBAween
candidates.summary: The Bell House's ABBA-meets-Halloween costume dance night, Friday Oct 30 at 8pm. It's on the venue's own schedule with tickets through Ticketmaster.
candidates.fit: He dressed up for an ABBA dance night in the West Village and loved it. This is that, plus Halloween costumes, in Gowanus instead of Manhattan — book it now and tell the group chat what to wear.

candidates.title: Nutcracker Rouge
candidates.time_text: evening showtimes vary; previews begin Nov 12
candidates.summary: Company XIV's adults-only holiday staple returns to Théâtre XIV for twelve weeks: previews begin Thursday Nov 12, 2026 and closing night is Saturday Jan 30, 2027. All tickets are on sale now; good dates and the champagne couches go first.
candidates.fit: The Nutcracker at Lincoln Center is his favorite night in the city and Company XIV is his favorite room — this is the two things welded together, ten minutes from Fort Greene. Book the good seats in October, not December.

candidates.title: George Balanchine's The Nutcracker — New York City Ballet
candidates.time_text: matinee and evening performances through the run
candidates.summary: NYCB's annual Nutcracker runs Friday Nov 27, 2026 through Saturday Jan 2, 2027 at the David H. Koch Theater. Tickets are already on sale per New York City Ballet's own site.
candidates.fit: He has said this is the single best thing he has done in the city, and Tchaikovsky's Nutcracker is literally in his Spotify library. The good December Saturdays disappear by Halloween, so this is a book-now item, not a December one.

candidates.title: Open House New York Weekend 2026
candidates.time_text: roughly 10am to 6pm Friday through Sunday, varies by site
candidates.venue: Open House New York (300+ sites citywide)
candidates.price_text: free at most sites; some reservation-only tours are ticketed
candidates.summary: OHNY unlocks more than 300 buildings, infrastructure sites and workshops across the five boroughs for three days of tours and open access. Most sites are free and walk-up; the best ones (power plants, water tunnels, private houses, stone-carving academies) require advance reservations that were released October 2.
candidates.fit: This is the one weekend a year you get inside rooms the city normally keeps shut, which is exactly his 'had to know someone' register, and the Brooklyn sites are mostly a bike ride from Fort Greene.

candidates.title: It Entirely From Memory
candidates.summary: A cast of comedians attempts to recreate the film 'It' live on stage with no script, no rehearsal and, per the venue, no sobriety. Thursday Oct 15, doors 7:30, show 8, 21+ at littlefield in Gowanus.
candidates.fit: Exactly the oddball-variety format he goes for — a bar back room doing something stupid and specific rather than a straight stand-up lineup. Thursday night, fifteen minutes from Fort Greene, out by 10.

candidates.title: Mr. Choade's Upstairs Downstairs
candidates.summary: The Slipper Room's Saturday night variety show — burlesque, sideshow, magic and circus acts in a small LES room that has been doing this since 1999. Oct 17 at 8pm, with a separate Midnight Show at 10:45pm if you want the dirtier late set.
candidates.fit: Small room, serious performers, no marketing budget — the Manhattan version of what Company XIV does, and a legitimate reason to be on Orchard Street instead of a Midtown rooftop. Pair the 8pm show with a drink at a real LES bar afterward.

candidates.title: Chris Gethard and Dave Ross Leave For Fest
candidates.summary: Gethard and Dave Ross work out festival material in Union Hall's basement room, Saturday Oct 17 at 7:30pm. Roughly 150 seats under a bar with bocce courts.
candidates.fit: Union Hall's back room is the closest thing to that Midtown apartment comedy show he loved — you're ten feet from the comic. Early enough that the guys can get a drink after and he's still home at a reasonable hour.

candidates.title: Asif Ali & Friends
candidates.summary: Asif Ali headlines a Saturday night showcase with guests at the Bell House, Oct 17 at 7:30pm. Standing-room Gowanus warehouse room, full bar, no two-drink minimum.
candidates.fit: A real headliner in a 300-cap Brooklyn room instead of an arena — the trade he always wants. Easy Saturday-night plan to propose to two or three friends.

candidates.title: Wunderkammer: A Taxidermy Showcase and Competition
candidates.summary: A live taxidermy showcase and judged competition at the Bell House, Thursday Oct 29 at 8pm. Listed on the venue's own schedule with tickets via Ticketmaster.
candidates.fit: This is the week's best 'you had to know someone to hear about it' item: a bar full of people judging stuffed animals, the Thursday before Halloween. Nobody in his group chat will have heard of it.

candidates.title: Kaiju Big Battel: Satan Sleeps Tonight
candidates.summary: Kaiju Big Battel is live costumed monster wrestling — guys in giant rubber suits destroying a cardboard city in a wrestling ring. Sunday Nov 1 at 6pm at the Bell House.
candidates.fit: He likes live pro wrestling in bars and he trains Muay Thai, so the joke lands harder for him than for most people. Sunday 6pm is a rare slot that actually works for a dad.

candidates.title: City of Gods Halloween Festival 2026
candidates.time_text: doors 9pm, runs to about 5am both nights
candidates.venue: City of Gods Festival at Industry City
candidates.summary: House of Yes's eighth annual two-night Halloween takeover of Industry City: multiple stages, Burning Man camps and art installations, costumes required for entry. Single-night and two-day passes available; Friday Oct 23 and Saturday Oct 24.
candidates.fit: The closest thing in New York to a warehouse night with actual production values — melodic house and techno across several rooms, built by the House of Yes crew, and a hard costume rule that keeps the bottle-service crowd out. This is a late one, so it's a once-a-year thing, not a weekly one.

candidates.title: REGGAE REWIND — Fall Edition
candidates.summary: Reggae Rewind's fall party takes over littlefield from 11pm Saturday Oct 17 until 4am, 21+. Reggae and dancehall selectors in a mid-size Gowanus warehouse room.
candidates.fit: His current phase is dancehall and Afrobeats — Popcaan, Sean Paul, Gyptian are all in the library — and this is the Brooklyn party version, not a listicle club. It peaks after midnight, so it's a sometimes night.

candidates.title: Karaoke Tremendous
candidates.price_text: free with RSVP on Eventbrite
candidates.summary: Union Hall's recurring late-night karaoke takeover of the downstairs room, Friday Oct 16 starting at 11:59pm. It repeats most Fridays — Oct 23 and Oct 30 are also on the calendar — and the Eventbrite listing is a free registration rather than a paid ticket.
candidates.fit: Interactive, free, and in a room small enough that singing is not a humiliation — the kind of thing he can propose as a nightcap after an earlier show. Fits the 'he participates' part of the brief.

candidates.title: Halloween Costume Comedy Show (comics perform in character)
candidates.summary: On Halloween night littlefield puts a lineup of comedians on stage in costume performing their sets entirely in character, hosted by Brittany Carney, with an audience costume contest and prizes. Doors 6:30, show 7:30, at 635 Sackett Street.
candidates.fit: Costume night plus a small room plus audience participation — three of his four sweet-spot criteria in one. An early Halloween show also leaves the rest of the night open.

candidates.title: Mr. Choade's Upstairs Downstairs Halloween Spooktacular
candidates.summary: The Slipper Room's Halloween-night edition of its Saturday variety show at 8pm, followed by a separate Halloween Midnight Show at 10:45pm. Burlesque, sideshow and circus acts in a small Lower East Side room.
candidates.fit: If he wants Halloween in Manhattan without going near the Village Parade crush, this is the move — a 150-ish seat room where the performers are the spectacle, not the crowd.

candidates.title: Lightscape at Brooklyn Botanic Garden
candidates.summary: BBG's mile-long after-dark illuminated trail returns Nov 20, 2026 through Jan 3, 2027 with a new route. Timed-entry tickets; peak weekend slots sell out well in advance, and there are 21+ nights as well as family slots.
candidates.fit: He has already done this one and liked it, which is exactly why it goes on the radar now — the December Saturdays and the 21+ nights are gone by November. Works as a stroller outing or as a date.

candidates.title: All Balanchine I — New York City Ballet
candidates.summary: NYCB's fall season closes out with an all-Balanchine program — La Sonnambula, Pithoprakta, The Unanswered Question and Theme and Variations — with matinee and evening performances on Saturday Oct 17. The season then ends Oct 18 with a farewell program for retiring principal Adrian Danchig-Waring.
candidates.fit: The Nutcracker was his best night in the city; this is the same company and the same house without waiting for December, and the Oct 18 farewell is a one-time thing. A clean date-night with the wife if they can get a sitter this weekend.

candidates.title: PRELUDE by Charles L. Mee, directed by Anne Bogart
candidates.price_text: free
candidates.summary: En Garde Arts reunites Anne Bogart and Charles L. Mee for a large-scale free outdoor performance on the BAM plaza, part of Next Wave 2026, running Oct 13–15. No ticket required.
candidates.fit: It is free, it is outdoors, and it is literally on the plaza he walks past — a zero-commitment Thursday that is still a real piece of theater rather than a street fair. Check BAM's page for the exact start time before committing.

candidates.title: Brett Goldstein Runs His Hour Before His Tour
candidates.summary: Brett Goldstein works out his full hour at the Bell House before taking it on tour, Wednesday Oct 21 at 7:30pm.
candidates.fit: A Wednesday is normally off the table, but this is the exception the rules allow: a name who will be playing theaters, doing the raw version in a 300-cap Gowanus room. Book it before it sells out.

candidates.title: Pizzazz with Gary Gulman
candidates.summary: Gary Gulman headlines the Pizzazz showcase in Union Hall's basement, Wednesday Oct 28 at 7:30pm. Capacity is roughly 150.
candidates.fit: A comic who sells out theaters, doing it in a room where he can see everyone's face — the thing he says he wants instead of arena comedy. Midweek, so only worth it because the room is this small.

candidates.title: Halloween Spooktackular
candidates.summary: A late Halloween-night comedy lineup in Union Hall's basement featuring Jenny Gorelick, Josh Nasser, Yoni Lotan, Ellen Harrold, Shaunak Godkhindi and Megasquirt. Saturday Oct 31 at 10pm.
candidates.fit: The backup plan for Halloween night if the earlier costume shows sell out, and a far better use of Oct 31 than standing on Sixth Avenue for the parade.

candidates.title: Diva Divination at Théâtre XIV (half off in October)
candidates.time_text: by appointment, before or around showtime
candidates.price_text: half off in October with promo code DIVINE50
candidates.summary: Company XIV runs tarot readings and 'French Kiss' lipstick readings by appointment at their Bushwick theater, and through the end of October they're half price with the code DIVINE50. The lipstick reading comes with a keepsake tube of Company XIV rouge.
candidates.fit: A ten-dollar-idea add-on that makes a Petite Rouge date night feel like he planned something, rather than just bought two tickets. Book it in advance for the same night as the show.

candidates.title: The Tiny Cupboard
candidates.time_text: stand-up every night; rooftop in warm weather, pink main room year-round
candidates.summary: A grassroots indie stand-up club in Bushwick founded by Amy Wong and Matt Rosenblum, built with no outside investors — it started in a 153-square-foot art studio, became a rooftop club in 2020, and now has an indoor main room plus a backyard board-game and video-game bar. Shows every single night, no drink minimum, all ages admitted.
candidates.fit: This is the 'you had to know someone' comedy room he keeps describing — tiny, community-built, no marketing budget, and cheap enough to try something random on a Thursday. The game bar out back gives the guys somewhere to sit afterward.

candidates.title: Wheels of NYC Car Show — Fall Edition
candidates.time_text: doors noon, runs through the afternoon
candidates.price_text: from about $50 on Dice
candidates.summary: Wheels of NYC takes over a 60,000 sq ft warehouse at the Brooklyn Navy Yard with 120-plus curated classic and modern cars, plus music, food and design vendors. Saturday Oct 17, noon start, tickets from roughly $50 on Dice. Organizer calls it their biggest edition yet.
candidates.fit: This is the Daikoku-style deep car scene he asked for, and it is a ten-minute walk from Fort Greene — an old Navy Yard warehouse full of air-cooled 911s and JDM builds, not a corny cruise-in. Daytime and warehouse-flat, so the 1-year-old can ride along in the carrier and stare at engines.

candidates.title: Beat Drop: DJ Takeover at Othership
candidates.time_text: two-hour session; start time shown at booking
candidates.summary: A two-hour sober-curious gathering in Othership's sauna and ice-bath space with a live DJ playing the room. Saturday Oct 17 at the Flatiron location. Price is not listed on the events index — it shows at the booking step.
candidates.fit: Sauna, cold plunge and a DJ who actually plays is the exact overlap of two things he already loves: a full bathhouse day and a good small room with proper sound. Easy Saturday-night plan with one or two of the guys that doesn't cost him Sunday morning with the kid.

candidates.title: Runners' Night x Vivobarefoot at Othership Williamsburg
candidates.time_text: evening; group run first, then sauna and ice
candidates.summary: A community group run that ends inside Othership's new Williamsburg location for heat, cold plunge and breathwork, run with Vivobarefoot. Tuesday Oct 13. Price appears at the booking step, not on the event index.
candidates.fit: A run club with an actual destination and a cold plunge at the end, not a dating app in sneakers — and it's in Williamsburg, where he's already going for Muay Thai at Kings Combat. Worth breaking the no-Tuesday rule if he wants to recce the new Othership before bringing friends.

candidates.title: Bathhouse Atlantic Avenue day pass
candidates.price_text: day pass from $29
candidates.summary: Bathhouse's third and newest location opened on Atlantic Avenue in 2026 with the biggest sauna in the system — a 100-plus-seat Event Sauna running complimentary Aufguss (guided towel-waving) sessions, plus cold plunges and steam. Day passes start at $29, the cheapest of the three Bathhouse locations.
candidates.fit: A full bathhouse day with a friend is one of his favorite things he's ever done in this city, and this one is a short ride from Fort Greene instead of a schlep to the East Village. The Aufguss sessions are the German sauna ritual done properly — heat, music, theater — which is a double hit for him.

candidates.title: Bathhouse Williamsburg — rooftop pool, banya and Event Sauna
candidates.price_text: day pass from $39; memberships $145/month (3 passes, $48 each) or $225/month (5 passes, $45 each)
candidates.summary: Bathhouse's Williamsburg flagship expanded in 2026 with a Russian-style banya, a new Event Sauna for its Aufguss program, and what it calls the largest rooftop pool in NYC. Eight thermal pools total: three hot, two cold plunges at 45 and 50 degrees, two neutral, one rooftop.
candidates.fit: He already knows Bathhouse, but the banya and rooftop pool are new since his last visit, which makes it a real plan rather than a repeat. Pair it with a Muay Thai session at Kings Combat around the corner and it's a whole Saturday with one friend.

candidates.title: Bike MS: New York City
candidates.price_text: registration fee plus a fundraising minimum — amount not confirmed
candidates.summary: The National MS Society's New York City ride returns Sunday Oct 18 with an early-morning start and multiple route distances. It's a charity ride, so there's an entry fee plus a fundraising minimum you have to hit before packet pickup. Start location and exact route mileage were not confirmed.
candidates.fit: He loved the Lower Manhattan-to-GWB ride with friends; this is the same kind of long waterfront morning with a real organizer and marshals instead of a group chat. Heads-up: the fundraising minimum means he'd need to sign up and hit it before Sunday, so this is a 'call the guys Monday' item.

candidates.title: Candlelit Restorative Free Flow at Othership Williamsburg
candidates.summary: A 75-minute candlelit sauna and ice-bath free flow built around rest rather than hype, Sunday Oct 18 at Othership Williamsburg. Runs regularly across their locations. Price shows at booking.
candidates.fit: The lower-key, slightly more polished version of his bathhouse day — a 75-minute block that works for a Sunday afternoon with his wife while the sitter covers the kid, no all-day commitment.

candidates.title: Mentalist Night: The Tell at Othership
candidates.summary: Mentalist Sawyer Bullock performs mind-reading inside the sauna at Othership's Yorkville location on Monday Oct 19. Small capacity by definition — it's a sauna. Price appears at booking.
candidates.fit: Magic in a 20-person sauna is exactly the 'you had to know about it' format he goes for, and it's close in spirit to the weird variety nights and apartment comedy shows he's loved. Monday and Upper East Side, so it only earns the trip because the premise is genuinely strange.

candidates.title: World Spa day pass
candidates.price_text: day passes from $99
candidates.summary: World Spa bills itself as NYC's largest day spa and banya, in Borough Park, with Russian banya, hammam, Finnish and other sauna styles, pools and restaurants across multiple floors. Day passes start at $99. Weekend slots sell out, so book ahead.
candidates.fit: This is the upgrade on the Russian & Turkish Baths day he loved — same banya logic, parilka and platza included, but a far bigger building and better food. A proper all-day guys plan where nobody has to talk about their week.

candidates.title: QC NY spa on Governors Island
candidates.summary: QC NY is the Italian-run spa in the restored officers' housing on Governors Island: saunas, steam rooms, indoor and outdoor pools and relaxation rooms, reached by a short ferry with skyline views the whole way. Day-pass pricing and October hours could not be confirmed for this report.
candidates.fit: Ferry with a destination plus a full sauna day is two of his favorite formats stacked together, and the island setting in mid-October keeps it from being a tourist thing. Flagging it as unverified: check the price and the ferry timetable on the site before committing.

candidates.title: TCS New York City Marathon — watching from Lafayette Avenue
candidates.time_text: lead runners through Fort Greene late morning; the crowd builds all afternoon
candidates.price_text: free
candidates.summary: The marathon's Brooklyn stretch runs straight down Lafayette Avenue through Fort Greene, traditionally the loudest spectating block of the whole course. Free, outdoors, no ticket. The NYRR site would not load for this report, so confirm the date and the course map before building a plan around it.
candidates.fit: It's literally his front yard, it's free, and it's the one day a year where standing on his own street with a coffee and the kid in the stroller is the plan. Good excuse to have three friends over first and walk out at 10.

candidates.title: Gowanus Open Studios 2026 (30th anniversary)
candidates.time_text: daytime both days; most studios open midday to early evening
candidates.address: Multiple studios around Gowanus, Park Slope and Carroll Gardens
candidates.price_text: free
candidates.summary: Arts Gowanus throws open 400 to 500 artists' working studios across Gowanus and into Park Slope and Carroll Gardens for its 30th year. Free, self-guided, and spread over roughly 90 buildings, several of which are being squeezed out by development. Several studios run their own beer-and-music open-house parties rather than polite gallery hours.
candidates.fit: This is the open-studio-party version of the friend's photo studio night he loved, at neighborhood scale and walking distance from Carroll Gardens. It also doubles as the family pick: stroller-friendly, free, and done by mid-afternoon if you want.

candidates.title: Clube do Choro with Regional Samauma (Sunday afternoon, front room)
candidates.price_text: donation at the door
candidates.summary: Every Sunday at 3pm, cavaquinho player Fernanda Silveira leads a Brazilian choro jam in the front room at Barbès with Regional Samauma and rotating guests. It is a jam, not a concert: acoustic, daylight, no stage, and the door opens to the street.
candidates.fit: Daylight, acoustic, no cover charge drama and a kid in a carrier is not a problem in the front room at 3pm. It is the family slot that is also genuinely good for the adults, and it is a short drive from Fort Greene.

candidates.title: Halloween at Barbès: Dionne Werewolf, Skalloween, and horror soundtracks at midnight
candidates.time_text: 8pm Dionne Werewolf, 10pm to midnight Pangari and the Socialites, DJ set at midnight
candidates.price_text: $20 suggested for the 10pm set; pay online or at the door
candidates.summary: Barbès runs its Halloween night as three acts: Dionne Werewolf, the city's werewolf orchestra playing Bacharach and Dionne Warwick, at 8pm; then Pangari and the Socialites doing classic ska, soul and rocksteady as 'Skalloween' from 10pm to midnight for $20 suggested; then WFMU's Roman Angelos spinning horror movie soundtracks at midnight.
candidates.fit: Costumes, a tiny room, a nine-piece ska band and a vinyl guy playing Italian horror scores is the Rocky Horror-in-Flatbush instinct done at bar scale, and it is Halloween on a Saturday.

candidates.title: America's Liberal Reckoning: A Munk Debate at 92NY (Fareed Zakaria and Patrick Deneen)
candidates.price_text: ticketed; price not confirmed
candidates.summary: The Munk Debates bring their Oxford-style format to 92NY with Fareed Zakaria arguing against Patrick Deneen on the state of American liberalism. Thursday night, in a real hall, with an audience vote before and after.
candidates.fit: This is the Open to Debate format he asks for with a genuine foreign-policy draw in Zakaria, on his main weeknight slot, and the audience vote makes it participatory rather than a lecture.

candidates.title: Mamady Kouyaté's Mandingo Ambassadors (weekly Wednesday residency)
candidates.price_text: cover collected at the door; amount not listed on the calendar
candidates.summary: Mamady Kouyaté, heir to a line of Guinean griots and a veteran of Bembeya Jazz, has held a weekly Wednesday residency at Barbès for years, playing the Syliphone-era Guinean sound with his Mandingo Ambassadors. It runs again on October 14, 21 and 28 at 10pm.
candidates.fit: West African guitar music played by the guy who actually made it in Conakry in the seventies, in a 60-seat back room, is the deep end of the Afro lane he is currently in. Wednesday is off his usual grid, but this one is worth breaking it for.

candidates.title: Festival Neue Literatur: Intimate Thresholds — Julia Franck and Nicole Krauss
candidates.price_text: registration required; price not listed
candidates.summary: The 16th Festival Neue Literatur pairs German novelist Julia Franck with Nicole Krauss, in conversation with translator Tess Lewis, for an evening of readings on identity and longing. It happens in the Deutsches Haus townhouse on Washington Mews, which seats well under a hundred.
candidates.fit: German literary culture and Jewish American literary culture in the same room, in a mews house most New Yorkers never walk into. It is a Monday, so it only earns a slot because both writers are real.

candidates.title: Brooklyn Maqam presents The Maqamposers Club
candidates.price_text: cover collected at the door; amount not listed on the calendar
candidates.summary: A new project dedicated to brand-new instrumental compositions by NYC-based composers working in Arabic maqam, with Alber Baseel on percussion, Gideon Forbes on ney, Sarah Mueller on violin, John Murchison on qanun and Zafer Tawil on oud. Brooklyn Maqam programs it; the room holds maybe sixty people.
candidates.fit: Word-of-mouth, community-run, no marketing budget, five serious players in a bar back room. This is the kind of thing he means when he says he wants the scene you had to know someone to hear about.

candidates.title: The Pre-War Ponies, then The Arntzen Family and Friends
candidates.price_text: cover collected at the door; amount not listed on the calendar
candidates.summary: Thursday at Barbès is a double header: Daria Grace's Pre-War Ponies playing forgotten Irving Berlin and Hoagy Carmichael sides at 7pm, then three generations of the Arntzen family (Evan on clarinet, Leif on trumpet, Miles Francis on drums) playing traditional jazz at 9pm.
candidates.fit: A cheap, unhyped Thursday where you can get a seat, hear the band without earplugs and talk to the bartender. Good fallback night out with one friend when nothing bigger is on.

candidates.title: Gili Yalo
candidates.price_text: cover collected at the door; amount not listed on the calendar
candidates.summary: Gili Yalo and band fuse traditional Ethiopian music with soul, funk, psychedelia and jazz, singing in English and Amharic. His story runs Ethiopia to Sudan on foot to Israel, and the music carries it. Friday night at Barbès, 8pm.
candidates.fit: Ethio-funk with a real rhythm section in a sixty-person room; it is the same Afro-diasporic lane as his amapiano and Afrobeats phase, just played live and loud. Also a date-night-sized Friday, not a 2am commitment.

candidates.title: Jenny Scheinman: All Species Parade
candidates.price_text: cover collected at the door; amount not listed on the calendar
candidates.summary: Violinist Jenny Scheinman, who has played with Bill Frisell, Jason Moran, Lucinda Williams and Lou Reed, returns to the room where she held a residency twenty years ago, with Carmen Staaf, Kenny Wollesen, Steve Cardenas and Tony Scherr. Two sets, 7pm and 9pm.
candidates.fit: A musician who could sell a much bigger room choosing to come back to a bar on 9th Street. That asymmetry is the whole appeal, and it is a Thursday.

candidates.title: Barbès Live Piano Karaoke with Allyssa Lamb
candidates.time_text: 7pm to 9:30pm, sign up in person that day
candidates.price_text: cover collected at the door; amount not listed on the calendar
candidates.summary: Barbès runs live piano karaoke on the second Thursday of every month, hosted by pianist and singer Allyssa Lamb of Las Rubias del Norte. You sign up in person that day and pick from a repertoire of over 100 songs, mostly pop and rock from 1955 to 1985. No screen, no backing track, just a piano.
candidates.fit: Interactive, small, and a format he can own with two friends: he picks the song, she plays it live. The second Thursday lands on November 12 next, which is also the Munk Debate night, so pick one.

candidates.title: Slavic Soul Party!
candidates.price_text: cover collected at the door; amount not listed on the calendar
candidates.summary: Balkan brass band Slavic Soul Party has played Barbès every Tuesday at 9pm for more than twenty years; the calendar literally lists it as 'every Tuesday, forever.' Nine horns and drums packed into a back room that holds about sixty people, and it gets sweaty.
candidates.fit: A Tuesday is off his grid, but this is the longest-running underground residency in Brooklyn and it is loud, physical and three stops from home. Bank it for a week when Thursday is dead.

candidates.title: Samuel Weber: Giving and Taking — Hamann's Metakritik of Kant
candidates.price_text: free; RSVP typically required
candidates.summary: Samuel Weber gives a public lecture on Johann Georg Hamann's counter-critique of Kant, in person at Deutsches Haus at NYU. Friday at 5:30pm in the Washington Mews townhouse.
candidates.fit: Only worth it if he is in the mood for proper German intellectual history rather than a panel; it is early enough on a Friday to do this and still get dinner. Deutsches Haus is also the place to get on the mailing list for the German family programming he wants.

candidates.title: Rabih Mroué and Lina Majdalanie: Four Walls and a Roof (North American premiere)
candidates.time_text: evening performances; exact times not confirmed
candidates.price_text: not confirmed
candidates.summary: The Goethe-Institut New York presents the North American premiere of a theatre piece by Lebanese artists Rabih Mroué and Lina Majdalanie over three nights, October 22 to 24. Listed on the institute's own events calendar under Dance and Theatre.
candidates.fit: Three performances only, presented by a cultural institute rather than a theatre company, which is usually how you end up in a room of eighty people watching something nobody will be able to see again. Verify the venue and curtain time before you commit.

candidates.title: Tammam Azzam: A Horizon Remains
candidates.price_text: free
candidates.summary: The Goethe-Institut New York is showing the first New York solo exhibition and first US institutional presentation of Syrian-born, Berlin-based artist Tammam Azzam, running September 16 to December 3, 2026. Free to walk into during gallery hours.
candidates.fit: A Berlin-based artist shown by the German cultural institute, free, and a twenty-minute stop rather than an afternoon. Good to stack with dinner on a Thursday rather than as the main event.

candidates.title: Haunted Carousel at Prospect Park
candidates.address: Flatbush Ave at Empire Blvd, Brooklyn, NY
candidates.price_text: free to attend; carousel rides ticketed
candidates.summary: NYC Parks lists a Haunted Carousel at the Children's Corner in Prospect Park on Sunday, November 1, noon to 5pm. The 1912 carousel gets decorated and costumes are the point.
candidates.fit: Day-after-Halloween, fifteen minutes from Fort Greene, over by mid-afternoon, and a 1-year-old on a wooden horse is a better photo than any playground. Confirm hours on the Parks page before you go.

candidates.title: The Rock and Roll Playhouse plays the Music of The Beatles for Kids
candidates.price_text: ticketed; price not confirmed
candidates.summary: A full band plays Beatles songs at noon on a Sunday at Brooklyn Bowl, with room on the floor for toddlers to wander, parachutes and bubbles, and a bar for the adults. Listed on Ticketmaster for November 29, 2026 at 12:00pm.
candidates.fit: He has a pile of Beatles in his library and a 1-year-old, and this is a real venue with a real PA rather than a library basement. It is in Williamsburg where he already trains, and you are out by 1:30.

candidates.title: CityKinder St. Martin's Lantern Walk in Prospect Park
candidates.venue: Prospect Park (near the Bandshell and the 9th Street playground entrance)
candidates.address: Prospect Park West at 9th Street, Brooklyn, NY
candidates.price_text: suggested donation per child in past years; 2026 amount not posted
candidates.summary: Every November the German-speaking community of Brooklyn gathers at dusk in Prospect Park with handmade lanterns, sings the traditional Laternenlieder, then processes through the park to a reenactment of St. Martin on horseback sharing his cloak. CityKinder organizes it as a fundraiser; registration is usually through Eventbrite.
candidates.fit: He plays Lichterkinder lantern songs with his kid already, so this is the one night a year those songs are sung out loud by a few hundred people a mile from his apartment. The 2026 date has not been posted yet, so watch the CityKinder page and register the day it opens; it sells out.

candidates.title: Razor-N-Tape presents "A Joyful Noise" — Live From Public Records album release show
candidates.summary: Resident Advisor lists a Razor-N-Tape album release show, 'A Joyful Noise,' at Public Records in Gowanus on Friday, October 23, 2026. Public Records' Sound Room is a roughly 150-capacity, audiophile-grade listening room on the Gowanus Canal. Price and set times were not readable from the listing.
candidates.fit: Small room, serious sound system, label-run night rather than a listicle event — exactly the Public Records register he likes, and a 15-minute hop from Fort Greene for a Friday with the guys.

candidates.title: DJ_DAVE at Elsewhere
candidates.summary: Songkick's Elsewhere venue calendar lists DJ_DAVE performing at Elsewhere in Bushwick on Friday, October 16, 2026. DJ_DAVE performs live-coded club music, so the set is built in front of the room rather than mixed from tracks. Room, ticket price and set times were not confirmed on the organizer page.
candidates.fit: Bushwick, small room, a DJ who is visibly making the music in front of you — the kind of club night he'd have to already know about, not something that tops a listicle.

laneReports.notes:
Hard constraints hit mid-research: the web_fetch tool stopped responding after ten page loads and web_search cut out shortly after, so a chunk of the lane is less verified than I'd like.

What IS verified (I read the organizer's own page and dates/venue matched): Company XIV (companyxiv.com and its tickets page — Petite Rouge extended through Halloween, Nutcracker Rouge previews Nov 12 through Jan 30 closing, October DIVINE50 promo), Union Hall's full Eventbrite-fed calendar, littlefield's calendar, the Bell House's schedule, the Slipper Room's calendar, Brooklyn Comedy Collective and The Tiny Cupboard.

PRICES ARE THE BIG GAP. None of the venue calendars I could load print ticket prices, and I could not open individual Eventbrite/Ticketmaster pages to confirm them. Rather than guess, I left price_text empty on most items. The only prices I'd state out loud: LIPS: Rocky Horror has been running roughly $52–$63 GA with tables much higher (from House of Yes's own listings for adjacent 2026 dates), and Union Hall's Karaoke Tremendous is a free Eventbrite registration rather than a paid ticket. Lightscape was $29–$44 in 2025; the 2026 price is not confirmed.

Unverified / flag in the email:
- PRELUDE at BAM (Oct 13–15): I have the dates and that it's free and outdoor on the plaza from BAM's Next Wave page copy and the season announcement, but NO start time. Tell him to check bam.org before walking over. I also couldn't get a specific event URL.
- NYCB: nycballet.com's own season page lists Fall 2026 as Sept 22–Oct 18 with All Balanchine I on Oct 17 (mat and eve) and the Adrian Danchig-Waring farewell Oct 18. A Time Out listing confusingly shows American Ballet Theatre at the same theater Oct 15–31, which looks like a stale 2025 page. I went with NYCB but marked it 'likely,' and I could not get an exact Nutcracker ticketing URL — the url field points at the season-and-tickets index.
- littlefield's Oct 31 in-character Halloween comedy show is from littlefield's own Instagram embed on their homepage (date, times, address, host, lineup, costume contest all stated). I could not find the individual ticket page, so the url is the all-shows index.
- Slipper Room's Oct 31 Halloween Spooktacular appears on their calendar grid but I couldn't extract the event-detail URL; it points at the calendar.
- City of Gods (Oct 23–24, Industry City): dates and the costumes-required rule are confirmed on House of Yes's own calendar entry, but I could not confirm current ticket prices or the lineup, which they said was still to be released.

Not covered, and worth chasing next week: Don't Tell Comedy New York (their city page returned empty on fetch and I ran out of search budget — their secret-location format is the single best match for the apartment show he loved, so it should be a standing item); Brooklyn Museum First Saturdays (the museum's own press release says the series runs the first Saturday of SELECT months, and I could not confirm whether November 7, 2026 is one of them — do not promise it without checking); Nitehawk and Alamo Drafthouse themed/costume screenings; Kings Theatre; live indie pro wrestling in Brooklyn; and current immersive theater. Brooklyn Comedy Collective's week was almost entirely student class shows, so I deliberately left it out.

Big caveat on method: the web_fetch tool hit its usage ceiling after the first handful of pages, and then the search tool capped out too, so coverage of this lane is thinner than it should be. What I did read directly: the Othership events index (all Othership items are date- and venue-verified from the organizer's own page — but that index does not print prices, so every Othership price_text is empty on purpose rather than guessed) and the World Spa homepage (day passes from $99). Wheels of NYC is marked verified because the Dice ticketing page content came back with the title, venue, Sat Oct 17 noon start and the from-price all matching the organizer's own listing. What failed or is unconfirmed: bathhouse.com blocks direct fetch and the live domain is abathhouse.com — the Atlantic Ave day-pass floor of $29 and the Williamsburg expansion details come from Bathhouse's own pages via search, not a direct read, and I could not confirm the Atlantic Ave street address. Bike MS NYC: date (Sun Oct 18) and ~7am start confirmed from two sources, but I could not confirm the start location, route distances, entry fee or the NYC-specific fundraising minimum — other 2026 Bike MS rides use $250-$275, so treat that as a ballpark only. Never loaded: TWA Hotel pool, ResortPass, Russian & Turkish Baths, Governors Island programming, bike.nyc local rides, Transportation Alternatives, NYRR races, Classic Car Club Manhattan, Union Garage, Jane Motorcycles. So no hotel-pool day pass, no night ride, no bouldering or open-mat item and no motorcycle-shop event this week — all of those are gaps to fill next run, not things that don't exist. Dead ends worth recording: Tour de Bronx 2026 already happened on Oct 4; Bike to the Beach NY was Oct 3; Bike New York's own calendar shows DHV is not running in 2026; Classic Car Club Manhattan has nothing public on Eventbrite or MotorsportReg; and there is no NYC equivalent of Daikoku running this window that I could find — the Daikoku searches all return Tokyo tours. Wheels of NYC at the Navy Yard is the closest thing and it is the strongest pick in the lane. Also skipped on taste grounds, though they are real and in-window: Othership's Singles Social x Tinder (Oct 16), Lovership (Oct 24) and Queer Night (Oct 14).

Fetch budget ran out early. I read the Barbès organizer calendar in full (their own October 2026 PDF, linked from barbesbrooklyn.com/events), so every Barbès item above is marked verified, with one caveat: the PDF has two weekday typos in the October 15–21 column (Cheo is labeled 'Friday 17' and one Mandingo listing 'Wednesday 16'); the day numbers are consistent with the rest of the calendar, so I used the dates, not the weekday labels. Barbès does not publish per-show ticket pages or door prices on the calendar, so I left price_text hedged rather than guess; some shows are donation-based and some have a strict door charge. The November Barbès calendar is not posted yet, so the piano karaoke date (second Thursday, November 12) is arithmetic from their own description, not a posted listing. After that, web_fetch and then web_search both hit a server tool-use limit, so everything non-Barbès is 'likely' or 'unverified' off organizer-site search snippets rather than pages I actually read end to end. What I could not reach at all: The Jewish Museum, Museum of Jewish Heritage, Center for Jewish History, and the Folksbiene season calendar — so the Jewish-culture lane here is thin and rests on the Nicole Krauss evening at Deutsches Haus. No klezmer in a small room landed inside this window; Barbès had Andy Statman on October 7 and Meshuganah Mambo on October 9, both already past. Also unreached: Columbia's Center on Global Energy Policy, Asia Society, Carnegie Council and Open to Debate, so there is no verified energy, LNG or commodities talk this week — the Munk Debate at 92NY on November 12 is the only serious ideas booking I can point to, and I could not read its ticket price. CFR's public events page only returned past events and most CFR meetings are members-only anyway. Deutsches Haus also has something on Thursday October 22 whose title was truncated in the snippet as 'Safeguarding Jud…' — likely relevant to the Jewish lane, worth a look at their events page. Goethe-Institut also lists a group show, 'Too Much Is Better Than Too Little,' October 8 to November 7, and a European Literature Night, both too vague in the snippet to include. Still open for next week: a German-run Oktoberfest, the Maccabee Bar Hanukkah pop-up return, Lightscape dates at Brooklyn Botanic, NYCB Nutcracker on-sale, and a car meet the toddler can walk through.

Straight answer: this lane came up almost empty and it is my fault, not the city's. My web search and fetch budget was cut off by a server-side tool-use limit after roughly two dozen calls, before I could read a single organizer page. Every subsequent search and fetch returned 'server tool use limit exceeded,' including retries after waiting. So nothing here is verified — I never got an organizer or ticketing page to render.

What I did establish before the cutoff, which is worth carrying into a re-run:

1) Instagram is effectively unsearchable through this index right now. site:instagram.com queries for @daikokunyc, @nonsensenyc and similar returned only profile landing pages (follower counts and bio text in og:description), never individual dated posts. The caption-level evidence this lane depends on was not reachable. If scraped posts can be supplied next week, this lane works; without them it degrades into a venue-calendar lane.

2) Important news for the melodic-house lane: on October 5, 2026 a New Jersey Superior Court judge ordered TCE Presents, the parent company behind Teksupport, to cease event operations amid a partner dispute (reported by Resident Advisor and EDM.com, week of Oct 7). Any Teksupport warehouse show in the next few weeks should be treated as at risk until the promoter confirms. Do not book one for him without checking.

3) Dead ends and things I saw but deliberately did not report: Kettama at Knockdown Center (Oct 8, already past); L7 at Knockdown Center Oct 24 (real, but nowhere near his taste); the League of Legends World Championship final at Barclays Center on Nov 14 (real and local, but esports is not in his profile); a 'House of Hallucinations' event page on the House of Yes calendar (calendar.houseofyes.org/e/xhautDzOXX) whose date I could not read, so I left it out rather than guess — it is almost certainly Halloween-season and is worth checking first on the re-run; Open House New York weekend, which the season notes flag and which Brooklyn sources reference for mid-October, but whose exact 2026 dates I could not confirm.

4) Venue calendars that need a direct fetch on the re-run, all of which blocked or returned empty for me: elsewherebrooklyn.com/events, nowadays.nyc, publicrecords.nyc, knockdown.center, houseofyes.org/calendar, and the RA club pages for Knockdown (ra.co/clubs/69401), Nowadays (ra.co/clubs/105873) and public records (ra.co/clubs/164270). RA and House of Yes both returned empty bodies through the fetcher, likely JS-rendered; Dice venue pages (dice.fm/venue/public-records-w2qg, dice.fm/venue/elsewhere-brooklyn-8p85) did surface in the index and are probably the better scrape target.

The two candidates above are from single search snippets. Both are plausible and both have a real URL, but neither should go in the email as a confident pick without someone opening the page first. Nothing was found this week on the car-meet, Muay Thai community, Afrobeats/dancehall, German or Jewish community fronts — not because it isn't out there, but because I ran out of calls.
